**Setup.** Let $p = 0.3$ (Frank wins a game) and $q = 0.7$ (Joe wins a game). The match ends when one player reaches 21 wins. If the loser has $k$ wins at the end ($0 \le k \le 20$), the match lasts $21+k$ games.

**Distribution.** Frank wins the match with $k$ Joe wins with probability $\binom{20+k}{k}p^{21}q^k$, and symmetrically for Joe. Therefore

$$E[N] = \sum_{k=0}^{20} (21+k)\left[\binom{20+k}{k}p^{21}q^k + \binom{20+k}{k}q^{21}p^k\right].$$

Since $(21+k)\binom{20+k}{k} = 21\binom{21+k}{k}$, this becomes

$$E[N] = 21\sum_{k=0}^{20}\binom{21+k}{k}\left[p^{21}q^k + q^{21}p^k\right].$$

**Binomial identity.** The sum $\sum_{k=0}^{20}\binom{21+k}{k}p^{22}q^k$ equals $P(\text{Bin}(42,p)\ge 22)$, because it counts the event that the 22nd success occurs within 42 trials. This gives

$$E[N] = 21\left[\frac{P(\text{Bin}(42,0.3)\ge 22)}{0.3} + \frac{P(\text{Bin}(42,0.7)\ge 22)}{0.7}\right].$$

**Check.** With $p=q=\tfrac12$ the same formula gives about 36.9, which matches the known scale for a first-to-21 match.

**Numerical values.**

- Let $X \sim \text{Bin}(42, 0.3)$. Then $P(X=22) \approx 1.2866\times10^{-3}$. Summing the tail with the ratio $P(X=k+1)/P(X=k) = \frac{42-k}{k+1}\cdot\frac{3}{7}$ gives $P(X \ge 22) \approx 0.0019978$.
- $P(X=21) \approx 3.1456\times10^{-3}$, so $P(X \ge 21) \approx 0.0051434$.
- $P(\text{Bin}(42,0.7) \ge 22) = P(X \le 20) = 1 - P(X \ge 21) \approx 0.9948566$.

**Combine.**

$$E[N] = 21\left[\frac{0.0019978}{0.3} + \frac{0.9948566}{0.7}\right] = 21\,[0.0066593 + 1.4212237] \approx 29.986$$

The expected number of games per match is about 29.99.

ANSWER: ≈ 29.99
